chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I do not see for the man that he should swear except by Allah.
And he said: The words of the man when he says 'No, by your adversary!', rather it is from the words of the Pre-Islamic period of ignorance.
And if the people were to swear by this, and the likes of it, it would neglect the swearing by Allah.

key_terms.قَوْلِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: words of the Pre-Islamic period of ignorance
key_terms.لَابَ: a common oath expression meaning 'No' or 'By God'

ai.seo_question: What is the proper way to swear an oath in Shia Islam and what are common oaths to avoid?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the exclusivity of swearing by Allah, critiquing the common practice of invoking one's adversary (shani') as a lingering remnant of Pre-Islamic ignorance (Jahiliyyah). He warns that the popularization of such colloquial oaths risks leading the community to neglect the proper, distinct act of swearing by Allah's name. This hadith underscores the theological importance of preserving divine names in speech and avoiding linguistic practices that dilute monotheistic reverence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Sama’at,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not see for the man that he should swear, except by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The words of the man where he is saying ‘No, by your adversary!’, so rather it is from the words of the Pre-Islamic period of ignorance,
and if the people were to swear by this, and the likes of it, it would neglect the swearing by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu from ‘Abd al-Karim from Sama‘ah who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘I say that
a man must take an oath and swear by Allah only.
People’s saying, la’ bal shane ’uka (no, but may your adversary be it) is of the expressions of the people of ignorance.’”
